title: GPU-accelerated FieldMatrix (HIP, dense matmul + SpMV)
description:
Device-resident `DFieldMatrix` on HIP/ROCm with on-device field arithmetic, matrix multiplication, and sparse matrix-vector product. Follow-on to the CPU linear-algebra epic `bb85c68a`. Explicitly **does not** cover factorizations (PLE, trsm, inv, solve) on device — those are a further follow-on. ## Status **Backlog / pre-filed.** Not ready for dispatch. Prerequisites: - [ ] `bb85c68a` complete (CPU `FieldMatrix` stack shipped). - [ ] `64c88ae4` complete (CPU benchmark baseline published). We need the CPU numbers before we can claim the GPU beats them. - [ ] User approval to dispatch breakdown. ## Primary goals 1. **Throughput-bounded dense + sparse ops on GPU.** `dgemm`-equivalent matmul and CSR SpMV, beating CPU past a measured size floor. 2. **Explicit host ↔ device transfers.** No hidden copies. Users choose when to go to device. 3. **Correctness parity with CPU.** Every device kernel cross-checks against its CPU counterpart on identical randomized inputs. 4. **Zero impact on non-ROCm builds.** Everything GPU stays behind `--features hip`. Default workspace build is unaffected. ## Scope - Device-side field arithmetic for `Fp

` (32- and 64-bit `P`), `Gf2_8`, `Gf2_16`, `Gf2_32`. - `DFieldMatrix` device-resident matrix type with explicit `to_device()` / `to_host()`. - Device matrix multiplication (`gemm`) with a measured crossover vs. CPU. - Device CSR SpMV. - Equivalence test harness: device kernel vs. CPU kernel on randomized inputs. - Extended benchmark harness (extension of `64c88ae4`'s container-pinned methodology) with a ROCm lane. Publishes CPU + GPU side-by-side. - Target architecture: gfx1030 (same as existing `gf2-kernels-hip` prototype). Others are a stretch. ## Non-goals - Factorizations on device (PLE, `trsm`, `trmm`, `trtri`, inv, solve) — future epic. - Characteristic / minimal polynomial on device — same reason. - NVIDIA support beyond what HIP's portability layer gives for free. - Unified memory / HMM — explicit copies only. - RNS for large primes on device — design reference in `dev/plans/dumas_pernet_takeaways.md` §1.3; implementation is a separate epic. - Replacing the CPU path for small matrices — CPU remains the default; GPU is opt-in past a measured size floor. ## Success criteria (preliminary; to be refined at breakdown) - [hard] Every device kernel passes equivalence tests against its CPU counterpart on randomized inputs across at least three fields (`Fp<65521>`, `Fp<2^31-1>`, `Gf2_16`). - [hard] `DFieldMatrix` H2D + D2H transfer is round-trip lossless and preserves field element semantics. - [hard] Device matmul beats CPU matmul past a measured size floor; that floor is documented in the benchmark publication. - [hard] Default workspace build (no `hip` feature) remains identical to today — verified by CI on a non-ROCm host. - [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review`, `doc-review` gates pass on every child story. - [hard] Benchmark methodology reuses `64c88ae4`'s container approach; ROCm layer pinned. - [aspirational] Within 2× of `hipBLAS` on `double`-equivalent throughput for `Fp

` matmul at n ≥ 1024. - [aspirational] Exceed CPU matmul throughput (GF(p), n = 2048) by ≥ 5×. ## Architecture sketch (informational; see design doc) - New crate: `gf2-core-hip` — depends on `gf2-core` and the existing `gf2-kernels-hip`. - Sibling to the CPU `FieldBackend`: a `FieldGpuBackend` trait carrying `gemm`, `spmv`, etc. - New associated trait `FieldDevice: FiniteField` provides the device representation (`DeviceRepr`), host↔device conversions, and a kernel vtable for core operations. ## Tentative story breakdown 1. Design `FieldDevice` trait + `DFieldMatrix` memory model (design-only). 2. Device `Fp

` Montgomery arithmetic + equivalence tests vs. CPU. 3. Device GF(2^m) carry-less multiplication + equivalence tests. 4. `DFieldMatrix` storage + H2D/D2H transfers. 5. Device matmul (`dgemm`) + criterion bench + measured crossover vs. CPU. 6. Device SpMV (CSR) + criterion bench. 7. Extended benchmark harness (GPU lane) + published run. ~3 waves when dispatched. ## Depends on - `bb85c68a` — CPU linear-algebra epic (must ship before this can start). - `64c88ae4` — CPU benchmark publication (baseline to beat). ## References - [GPU FieldMatrix sketch](dev/plans/gpu_fieldmatrix_sketch.md) — this epic's design doc. - [fflas-ffpack analysis](dev/plans/fflas_ffpack_analysis.md) — CPU baseline patterns. - [Dumas–Pernet takeaways](dev/plans/dumas_pernet_takeaways.md) — algorithmic guidance, especially §1.3 (RNS for large primes — out of scope for this epic but referenced for future work).
